newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen easing this week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen easing this week.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to ease at auctions in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety said in its weekly market preview.

Wesfarmers said this week's expected further softening is due to an extra 12,688 bales nationally being put up for auction, mainly by growers who had previously withheld wool. About 110,568 bales in all will be on offer.
"However, there are signs of an improvement in buyer activity at prices not too far below these levels, largely due to expectations of limited supply over the longer term," Wesfarmers said.
In the week after next, there are no sales nationally and beyond May, the roster returns to much smaller offerings, it said.
"This indicates that although further easing is expected next week, prices will consolidate and reach levels of support," it said.
Last week's eastern market indicator fell 18 cents to 660 cents per kg clean, nearly reversing a 19 cents rise the previous week.
